  MANIPAL ACADEMY OF HIGHER EDUCATION  
  FIFTH SEMESTER B.TECH. (INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY) EXAMINATIONS - NOVEMBER 2024  
  SUBJECT: ICT 3123/ICT_3123 - SOFTWARE ENGINEERING  
  SOFTWARE ENGINEERING [ICT 3123]  
Marks: 50                                                                                                     Duration: 180 mins.  
  
  A  
Answer all the questions.  
  
1A)               Suppose you are leading a software development project for a new mobile application aimed at         (5)  
  fitness tracking. Considering the requirements of the project and the target timeline, analyze which  
  software process model would be most suitable for this project. Justify your choice by discussing at  
  least three key factors that influence your decision.  
1B)               Illustrate some of the common risks encountered in testing projects and their characteristics.          (3)  
1C)               Illustrate with an example, the different metrics used for Object Oriented Testing.                     (2)  
2A)               Your team is tasked with designing a mobile application for a ride sharing service. How would you       (5)  
  use scenario-based modeling to identify key features of the applications and create the use cases  
  for the above scenario.  
2B)               You are assigned as a business analyst for a software project to develop an online learning             (3)  
  platform. Conduct a requirement analysis for this project by identifying and categorizing at least five  
  functional and five non-functional requirements. Discuss the importance of each category in the  
  context of the project.  
2C)               Why doesn't everyone prove that a software component or program is correct?                             (2)  
3A)               Imagine you are responsible for developing a collaborative project management tool with the             (5)  
  following essential features:  
  
  Real-time document editing and sharing  
  Task assignment and tracking for team members  
  Integrated communication channels (chat and video calls)  
  User role management with customizable permissions  
  Mobile and desktop compatibility for seamless access  
  
  Your design should consider data security and user experience. Discuss the architectural style &  
  strategy you would implement to ensure the tool is both efficient and user-friendly.  
3B)               A student registration class as methods : adding a class, dropping a class, transferring to a different (3)  
  section of the class and list classes. A student must first be registered with the university (opened  
  as a student). Holds can be placed on a student and this effects whether he/she can register for a  
  class. There are limits on how many credit hours a student may register for. A student may  
  graduate (close a student). Identify what testing techniques can be used for testing the above  
  example application and design suitable test suite.  
3C)               Analyze the impact of the following on software application development in terms of maintainability, (2)  
  scalability, and user satisfaction:  
  i) The number of modules in a software project  
  ii) Functionality or services to be provided by the software application

4B) Evaluate the core practices and principles of Extreme Programming (XP) and their impact on (3)  
software development.  
4C) Imagine you are tasked with designing an online event management platform with the following key (2)  
features:  
e Event scheduling and calendar integration  
e Ticket purchasing and registration management  
« Attendee networking capabilities (e.g., chat and forums)  
e Real-time updates and notifications  
e Analytics dashboard for event organizers  
Your design should prioritize maintainability and user engagement. Discuss the design principles  
you would apply to ensure the platform is scalable and user-friendly.

5B)   Create a requirement specification consisting of list of objects, services/functions, constraints, and (3)  
  performance criteria for the following scenario:  
  A Library Management System (LMS) is implemented in a public library, comprising various objects  
  including book records that contain titles, authors, genres, and availability status; member profiles  
  that include personal information and borrowing history; staff profiles detailing roles and  
  responsibilities; and inventory management for tracking available books and resources. The LMS  
  offers services such as member registration for new patrons, book checkout and return for  
  managing borrowed items, reservation systems for holding books, and catalog searching to find  
  available titles easily.This system is subject to constraints such as data privacy to protect sensitive  
  member information, compliance with copyright laws regarding book lending practices, resource  
  availability to ensure that popular titles are adequately stocked, scalability to handle increasing  
  membership, and interoperability to integrate with external systems like online databases or e-book  
  platforms. The LMS aims to enhance user experience by providing efficient access to library  
  resources while ensuring that the library operates smoothly. It must also address the challenges of  
  managing large volumes of data related to books and members while maintaining high levels of  
  performance and security.  
5C)   Examine the steps involved in risk identification and their importance in the early stages of project (2)  
  planning. Illustrate how using a risk item checklist, questionnaire, risk components, and drivers can  
  contribute to a comprehensive risk identification process.
